autoAutomaticallyTagYourLocalAudioFilesF:
Automatically tag your local audio files, from several online platforms, based on {artist} & {title} tag, filename or playlist.
Or identify tracks with {shazam}. {videoTutorial}
autoItReadsTheTagFromYourLocal:
It reads the {artist} & {title} tag from your local MP3, AIFF, FLAC & M4A files (or filename or playlist),
feeds it into the search engine of the selected platforms, fetches the tags & writes it to your files.

When no tags or proper filename is present, you can enable {shazam} to identify the track & still fetch tags.
{beatport}, {junoDownload} & {traxsource} are based on a method called scraping.
{beatsource}, {itunes} & {musicbrainz} are based on their API. {discogs} & {spotify} too, but need a free account.
autoFetchesMetadataAutomaticallyWritesTa: Fetches metadata automatically & writes tags to your audio files. Fully configurable. Set to overwrite or add/fill in when empty.

audioAutomaticallyTagYourLocalAudioFiles: Automatically tag your local audio files, with so called audio features by {spotify}, based on {value} tag or exact match. {videoTutorial}
audioSelectAFolderWithTracksYouWant:
Select a folder with tracks you want to get their audio features fetched for - or drag & drop playlist.
Based on the {isrc} inside the metadata it will search up the track in Spotify's API & return these values.
If no {value} tag exists, it will search on {artist} & {title} tag by exact match.
Prominent tag translates the raw values from {value2} to a meaningful #description.

quickManuallyTagYourLocalAudioFilesQuick:
Manually tag your local audio files quickly, based on {energy}, {mood}, {genre} & other characteristics you defined.
Key bind compatible for quick access. {videoTutorial}

Decide in which tag you want them to write, so you are able to read them out in your favorite DJ software.

Also predefine where to write the energy rating by selecting a proper tag frame.

It reads the metadata of MP3, AIFF, FLAC & M4A files within a folder.
You can review what tags got written where inside the metadata, edit them, add a new tag or delete.
editorAListOfAllAudioFilesWithin: A list of all audio files within the folder will be populated.

editorThePathSelectedInWillOverwriteThe:
The path selected in {quickTag} will overwrite the path of {editTags} & vice versa.
This way it becomes easy to review where your custom tags got written, by switching between the two tabs.
editorInsteadOfWhichMatchesAutomatically:
Instead of {autoTag}, which matches automatically based on best match,
{manualTag} allows you to be more specific and select the result you want.
This might come in handy when you are tagging a certain album or release.
editorTheTrackYouWantToSearchUp: {click} the track you want to search up and click {manualTag} at the bottom.
editorSelectThePlatformsAndTagsYouWant: Select the platforms and tags you want to seek for and hit {start}
editorAListOfResultsWillShowUp: A list of results will show up that matches the {artist} + {title} and/or {value} of your track.

Tip: To check if this is the proper release more thorough, {click} the {externalLinkIcon} icon to go to the URL.
It will open the link of the fetched result in your browser.

When a track is selected, it will also show this as a button in the custom tags panel on the right, at the bottom.
